evidence: Nep. Att. 14.3: omnisque ejus pecūniae reditus cōnstābat in Ēpīrōticīs et urbānīs possessiōnibus
Plin. Ep. 2.4.3: reditus propter condiciōnem agellōrum nesciō minor an incertior
terms.comment: Literally a coming back: what money or land brings in. In this sense not in Cicero, but in Nepos, Ovid, Livy and Pliny’s letters (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Par. 49: ex meō tenuī vectīgālī, from my modest income
terms.comment: Properly a tax paid to the state; Cicero uses it of his own rents and income.

terms.gloss: the yield of land or capital; income
terms.comment: What a property produces, in kind or in money.

phrases.latin: omnisque ejus pecūniae reditus cōnstābat in Ēpīrōticīs et urbānīs possessiōnibus
phrases.english: and all his income came from his properties in Epirus and in the city

phrases.latin: Ex meō tenuī vectīgālī dētractīs sūmptibus cupiditātis aliquid etiam redundābit.
phrases.english: From my modest income, once the costs of greed are taken off, there will even be something left over.

sources: Lewis & Short: reditus · Lewis & Short: vectigal · Lewis & Short: fructus
